originalThought: QUELLE (Long 1862): 6.54 'That which is not good for the swarm, neither is it good for the bee'; 2.1 'we are made for co-operation, like feet, like hands...'. What harms the whole harms the part.
softwareInterpretation: INTERPRETATION: A module should fit into the whole: clear, directed, necessary dependencies — no cycles, no superfluous coupling, no violation of the declared architecture direction.
preconditions: An import/module graph is resolvable (limited dynamic imports/reflection).
limits: 'Superfluous' sometimes needs domain judgment; dynamic imports/DI can be invisible to static analysis.
counterexamples: High but directed fan-in onto a deliberately central utility.
A dependency explicitly permitted by the architecture.
